records.region: Northern Greenland, Inland Ice south of Freuchen Land and the southern Freuchen Land ice/rock setting.
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river identity established. Freuchen Land is a land-region context label only.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The actual complete national original covers the entire selected Inland Ice opening, westward corridor, northern ice/rock transitions and actual southern Freuchen Land ending. The regional original independently exposes the opening before its western map edge. This complete geographic coverage does not establish one representative named natural river or substantiate a conventional river mouth.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected object begins on the Inland Ice, runs briefly north, turns west through many short stored parts, bends northwest and then continues north into the southern Freuchen Land terrain. The actual ending is within the ice-covered setting depicted there on the national map. The more northerly J. P. Koch Fjord and the separate Hans Tavsens Iskappe are neighboring context features, not demonstrated terminal or representative river names.
records.completion_scope: All 36 stored parts, including the headward opening, every intermediate join, the regional-map edge crossing, all westward bends, the final northward ice/rock passage and the actual rendered endpoint were compared with readable original cartography. No substantial geographic interval is unviewed at ordinary source scale. Exact contemporary ice-front, bank, shore, channel and hydraulic positions remain outside the bounded conclusion.

component_scope_limits: Freuchen Land is a land-region label; Hans Tavsens Iskappe and J. P. Koch Fjord are neighboring ice-cap and fjord features. None is a supported whole-system river hydronym.
Ice surface contours, ice-thickness isopachs, contours of sub-ice bedrock and geological contacts do not prove a river channel or hydraulic connection.
The modeled terminal category is not independent evidence of an ordinary river mouth. The source reading reaches the actual endpoint in the historical ice-covered terrain.
Historical cartography does not establish modern drainage or exact ice/shore positions.
A null candidate means no name was established here; it does not assert that no local or official name exists.

records.region: Northern Alaska: Pogopuk Creek–Kavik River–Shaviovik River–Mikkelsen Bay corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-river/system identity for the selected connected Pogopuk Creek–Kavik River–Shaviovik River route to Mikkelsen Bay. Distinct upstream creek and river names are retained; Shaviovik River is not asserted as the scalar name of every selected position.
records.completion_scope: Four overlapping original maps were visually inspected across all 25 stored parts of the single selected mainstem, including the chosen opening, named confluences, branching plain corridor, wetlands, delta and actual eastern coastal terminal. Connected mapped channels establish ordinary representative-system correspondence without a material unread or missing through-link interval. Local floodplain and delta cutoffs are retained as generalization limits. No through-lake, managed or glacial connector is required by this selection.
records.supported_name_scope: Pogopuk Creek in the upper mountain valley; Kavik River after the upper confluence and through most of the coastal plain; Shaviovik River after its lower western confluence and through the delta; Mikkelsen Bay is the receiving coastal waterbody.

records.region: Northwestern Baffin Island, Nunavut, Canada; Magda River–Jungersen Bay corridor.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the connected selected eastern feeder–Magda River route to Jungersen Bay. The unlabelled opening and minor upstream links are not assigned Magda as a uniform scalar name.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system research using the independently issued original field-study maps and prose. No material selected-route through-link is left unresolved at the requested regional/corridor scale. The supported name remains a research candidate, with accepted/product fields null or false.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the connected selected eastern feeder–Magda River route to Jungersen Bay. The unlabelled opening and minor upstream links are not assigned Magda as a uniform scalar name.

naming_scope_details.unnamed_components: The eastern feeder and minor upstream connecting reaches have no separately established names in this pass.
naming_scope_details.no_unnamed_claim: An unestablished local component name does not mean that no Inuit, local or official name exists.

records.region: Southern Alabama and northwestern Florida: Lightwood Knot Creek–Yellow River–Blackwater Bay corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: Yellow River is the supported representative identity of the connected system, including the selected Lightwood Knot Creek approach, its mapped impoundment passage, downstream Yellow River trunk and connected delta to Blackwater Bay. Component names, impoundment scope and local delta names remain distinct; this is not a whole-feature natural-river scalar.
records.completion_scope: All 60 supplied parts of the one selected fragment were considered against four overlapping readable original maps. The chosen creek opening, impoundment through-passage and outlet, Lightwood–Yellow junction, every intermediate corridor and selected part join, state-line reach, Yellow–Shoal junction, lower wetland/side-channel connections and actual Blackwater Bay terminal are established at ordinary corridor scale. Distinct component names are compatible with the bounded representative Yellow River identity. Exact banks, individual coarse-line-to-distributary allocation, current flow and formal name-boundary vertices are outside this finding.
records.supported_name_scope: Yellow River is the supported representative identity of the connected system, including the selected Lightwood Knot Creek approach, its mapped impoundment passage, downstream Yellow River trunk and connected delta to Blackwater Bay. Component names, impoundment scope and local delta names remain distinct; this is not a whole-feature natural-river scalar.

scope_limits: Formal registry identity, Korean forms and exact hydronym transition vertices remain unverified.
The impoundment near Opp is established cartographically, but a separately verified lake/reservoir name and present operations are not claimed.

The lower delta contains distinct named channels and lakes. The coarse selected line is matched at ordinary connected-delta scale without assigning every vertex to a present individual channel or replacing local names.
Map labels, channel depiction and wetland connections do not establish current flow, tidal direction, seasonal discharge or exact contemporary banks.
The rendered length is a modeled measure, not an official named-river length.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
